title: How to Run an IB Parent Information Evening
summary: Plan an effective IB parent information evening with a clear agenda, accurate DP explanations, practical examples, and answers to common questions.
body_markdown:
An effective **IB parent information evening** should leave families understanding how the Diploma Programme works, what the school expects, and how parents can provide appropriate support. The strongest events combine an accurate whole-group presentation with school-specific guidance, practical examples, student perspectives, and time for questions.


Parents should leave with written resources, named contacts, and clear next steps. They do not need every detail of IB policy in one evening, but they should understand the decisions and responsibilities that will shape DP1 and DP2.


### Decide what parents should know and do


Define the intended outcomes before building slides. By the end of the session, parents should be able to:


- Describe the six-subject structure and the DP core.
- Distinguish **Higher Level (HL)** from **Standard Level (SL)** .
- Explain how subjects, TOK, the Extended Essay, and CAS contribute to the Diploma.
- Identify school deadlines and appropriate support contacts.
- Understand acceptable parental involvement in coursework.
- Check subject choices against possible university requirements.
- Recognize when academic, organizational, or wellbeing support is needed.


This focus prevents the event from becoming a lecture about IB history. Introduce the programme's educational purpose briefly, then concentrate on the practical questions families will face.


### Suggested agenda for an IB parent information evening


A **75-minute** session is usually sufficient for a general introduction. Adapt the timing to your school, and arrange translated materials or interpretation when needed.


Time Agenda item Main content


0-5 minutes Welcome Introduce the DP team, outcomes, and question process.


5-15 minutes Diploma overview Explain six subjects, HL and SL, the core, and the two-year structure.


15-25 minutes Subject selection Present available courses, prerequisites, combination rules, and university considerations.


25-35 minutes Assessment and points Cover examinations, coursework, internal assessment, grades 1-7, and the 45-point maximum.


35-45 minutes TOK, EE, and CAS Explain purpose, assessment, milestones, and completion requirements.


45-55 minutes Student experience Show a sample week and assessment calendar, ideally with a student perspective.


55-65 minutes Support and integrity Identify support routes, inclusion procedures, and boundaries for parental help.


65-75 minutes Questions Answer general questions and explain follow-up arrangements.


If subject selection is the main purpose, add consultation tables afterward so families can speak with teachers, the coordinator, and university counsellors.


### Explain the IB Diploma accurately


The[official DP curriculum overview](https://ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/curriculum/) shows that students study six subjects alongside the core. Full Diploma students normally take **three or four subjects at HL** , with the remainder at SL. The IB recommends **240 teaching hours for HL** and **150 for SL** .


The core contains three components:


- **Theory of Knowledge (TOK):** An exploration of how knowledge is produced, justified, and challenged. Assessment includes an exhibition and a **1,600-word essay** .
- **Extended Essay (EE):** An independent research project culminating in a paper of up to **4,000 words** .
- **Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS):** Sustained experiences across three strands. CAS earns no points, but successful completion is required.


HL does not automatically make a subject more valuable. HL courses have greater scope and teaching time, but both HL and SL subjects receive grades from **1-7** and contribute equally to the numerical total.


### Make the points system concrete


Use one calculation rather than describing the system abstractly.


Component Example result


Six subject grades 6 + 6 + 5 + 5 + 5 + 4 = 31


TOK and EE core points 2


Diploma total 33 out of 45


The maximum is **45 points** , consisting of 42 subject points and up to three points from TOK and the EE. The[official DP passing criteria](https://ibo.org/about-the-ib/what-it-means-to-be-an-ib-student/recognizing-student-achievement/about-assessment/dp-passing-criteria/) require at least **24 points** , but 24 alone does not guarantee the Diploma. CAS completion, minimum HL and SL performance, and other conditions also apply.


### Explain assessment and workload


The Diploma does not depend entirely on final examinations. Written examinations are central in most subjects, while assessment may also include investigations, oral work, performances, projects, and coursework.


Clarify that **internal assessment** does not mean the classroom teacher has complete control over the final result. Teachers mark certain components, and the IB moderates samples to maintain consistent standards. Other coursework is externally assessed, so families should use current school and subject information rather than generic percentages found online.


Show the school's two-year calendar for IAs, TOK, the EE, CAS reviews, mock examinations, and university applications. A calendar explains workload more honestly than assigning one weekly homework figure to every student.


### Connect subjects to university entry


Do not promise that the Diploma guarantees admission, credit, or advanced standing. Requirements are determined by universities and national authorities and may change. Families should consult the[IB university recognition database](https://ibo.org/university-admission/find-countries-and-universities-that-recognize-the-ib/) and official university pages.


Recommend this decision sequence:


1. Identify plausible degree areas.
2. Check required subjects, levels, grades, and total scores.
3. Compare these requirements with the school's subject menu.
4. Consider the student's attainment, interests, and sustainable workload.
5. Confirm the combination with the coordinator or counsellor.


The most demanding-looking combination is not necessarily the strongest. Appropriate choices preserve relevant options while allowing consistent performance.


### Define the parent's role


Parents can support routines, sleep, communication, and deadline planning. The[RevisionDojo IB parent checklist](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-parent-checklist-by-year) provides stage-specific prompts from DP1 through results.


Parents must not research, write, rewrite, analyse, or commission assessed work. The IB's[academic integrity policy](https://www.ibo.org/contentassets/76d2b6d4731f44ff800d0d06d371a892/academic-integrity-policy-english.pdf) supports parental involvement in manageable planning while prohibiting unauthorized assistance. A useful principle is **support the process, never supply the product** .


The[RevisionDojo guide for IB parents](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/revisiondojo-for-ib-parents) explains how Study Notes, Flashcards, the Questionbank, Mock Exams, and Jojo AI can supplement school teaching. External tools must still be used within school rules and cannot replace teacher feedback.


### Address inclusion and common mistakes


Explain inclusion procedures before individual concerns arise publicly. The[IB access and inclusion policy](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/programmes/dp/pdfs/access-and-inclusion-policy-en.pdf) states that arrangements should reduce barriers without changing what students are expected to learn. Eligibility, supporting evidence, the student's usual way of working, and application deadlines may all matter, so families should contact the school early.


Avoid these common presentation errors:


- Presenting 24 points as the only Diploma condition.
- Describing CAS as optional because it carries no points.
- Promising universal university recognition or credit.
- Giving one workload estimate for every subject combination.
- Allowing individual cases to dominate the general question period.
- Sharing policies without explaining the next action.


Use an anonymous question form and send a consolidated response afterward.


### Materials to send after the event


Provide the slides, a one-page overview, the subject-choice guide, a two-year calendar, relevant school policies, deadlines, and contact details. Include the[official IB guide for parents](https://ibo.org/diploma-guide/) and[RevisionDojo's explanation of the Diploma Programme](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/what-is-the-ib-diploma-programme) .


Collect brief feedback about what became clearer, what remains unclear, and which follow-up sessions families need.


### Conclusion


A successful IB parent information evening translates programme rules into practical decisions. Explain the structure and points accurately, make workload visible, connect subjects to university requirements, and establish clear boundaries for parental support. Official IB resources should remain the basis for policy, while RevisionDojo Study Notes, the Questionbank, and Jojo AI can provide supplementary clarification and practice.
